$comment: The versioned contract between Praxis Kit diagnostics and any message catalog. A language pack is validated against this file, not against English. See docs/localization/authoring-language-packs.md.

kinds.identifier: A name or token from HTML, ARIA or the author's own code (an element, attribute, role, component or variant). Copy it verbatim; never translate it.
kinds.literal: A value shown as source text. Copy it verbatim.
kinds.number: A number. May select a plural form when the entry names it as its plural selector.
kinds.string[]: A list of identifiers or literals. Join it with a list filter (`list`, `list-or`, `list-unit`), optionally after `quote`.
kinds.text: Prose written in English by Praxis Kit. None exist in contract 1: prose is never passed in context.

HTML3002.description: An element has `role=""`, an explicit but empty role. The attribute does nothing, so it should be removed.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

HTML3003.description: An element is given a `role` that is already its implicit (native) role, such as `role="navigation"` on `<nav>`. The attribute is redundant.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

implicitRole.description: The ARIA role an element has by default, for example `navigation` for `<nav>`.

HTML3004.description: An element with a fixed native role is given a different role (for example `role="region"` on `<nav>`), which overrides its meaning for assistive technology.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

implicitRole.description: The ARIA role an element has by default, for example `navigation` for `<nav>`.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

HTML3005.description: An element that is already a self-contained landmark is given `role="region"`. The role has been removed.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

implicitRole.description: The ARIA role an element has by default, for example `navigation` for `<nav>`.

HTML3006.description: An element with a fixed landmark role is given a different role. The override confuses assistive technology and has been removed.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

implicitRole.description: The ARIA role an element has by default, for example `navigation` for `<nav>`.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

HTML3007.description: An element is a direct child of a parent that does not allow it. The parent accepts the listed tags.

child.description: The offending child element, written as a tag such as `div`.

parent.description: The parent element, written as a tag such as `ul`.

allowed.description: What the parent accepts: tags written like `<li>`, as a list.

HTML3007.phrasing.description: An element is a direct child of an `<a>` but is interactive content, which an anchor does not allow. The parent accepts phrasing content.

child.description: The offending child element, written as a tag such as `div`.

parent.description: The parent element, written as a tag such as `ul`.

HTML3007.unspecified.description: An element is a direct child of a parent that does not allow it. The parent has no simple list of accepted tags.

child.description: The offending child element, written as a tag such as `div`.

parent.description: The parent element, written as a tag such as `ul`.

HTML3008.description: An explicit `role` is not one of the roles that ARIA in HTML allows on this element. The allowed alternative roles are listed.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

allowedRoles.description: The roles allowed on the element, as a list.

HTML3008.none.description: An explicit `role` is not allowed on this element, and ARIA in HTML allows no alternative role for it at all.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

allowedRoles.description: The roles allowed on the element, as a list.

HTML3101.description: An `<input>` has a `type` that is not defined by the HTML specification. Browsers fall back to `type="text"`, so it is usually a typo.

HTML31xx.attributeIgnored.description: An `<input>` has an attribute that only applies to some input types, but its `type` is not one of them, so the browser ignores the attribute. One id serves all fourteen attribute codes (HTML3102 to HTML3115).

attribute.description: An HTML attribute name, for example `size`.

allowedTypes.description: The input types the attribute applies to, as a list.

HTML3201.description: An `<a>` has an `href` using a scheme that executes content when navigated to (`javascript:`, `data:` or `vbscript:`). The `href` has been removed.

ARIA2003.description: An `aria-*` attribute is not valid on the element's role. It will be removed.

key.description: The ARIA attribute that is not valid on this role.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

ARIA2004.description: An element has a live-region role but no `aria-live`. The politeness level implied by the role has been added.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

impliedLive.description: The `aria-live` value implied by a role, for example `polite`.

ARIA2005.description: An element has a live-region role and no `aria-atomic`. Whether the whole region or only changed nodes is announced is left to the browser.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

ARIA2006.description: `aria-relevant` contains tokens that are not valid (valid: additions, removals, text, all).

ARIA2007.description: `aria-relevant` combines `all` with other tokens. `all` already includes everything, so it should be used alone.

ARIA2008.description: The element has an ARIA role that is not recognised, or not applicable to it. The role will be ignored by assistive technology.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

ARIA2009.description: An element that needs an accessible name has none. Only reported when a rule that requires a name is enabled (for example for a repeated landmark).

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

ARIA2010.description: An `aria-*` attribute is set on an element that is presentational (`role="none"` or `role="presentation"`). Presentational elements are hidden from assistive technology, so the attribute has no effect.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

ARIA2011.description: `aria-hidden="true"` is set on a focusable element. Keyboard users can reach it but assistive technology cannot describe it.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

ARIA2012.description: A role requires a state or property that is missing (for example `aria-expanded` on `role="combobox"`).

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

ARIA2013.description: An `aria-*` attribute has a value that is not valid. The valid values are a fixed set, listed.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

got.description: The value that was given, already rendered as source text (strings are quoted; `null` and `undefined` are spelled out). Do not add quotes around it.

values.description: The allowed values, as a list.

ARIA2013.number.description: An `aria-*` attribute needs a number and was given something else.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

got.description: The value that was given, already rendered as source text (strings are quoted; `null` and `undefined` are spelled out). Do not add quotes around it.

ARIA2013.integer.description: An `aria-*` attribute needs an integer and was given something else.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

got.description: The value that was given, already rendered as source text (strings are quoted; `null` and `undefined` are spelled out). Do not add quotes around it.

ARIA2013.integerMin.description: An `aria-*` attribute needs an integer that is at least a minimum and was given something else.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

got.description: The value that was given, already rendered as source text (strings are quoted; `null` and `undefined` are spelled out). Do not add quotes around it.

ARIA2013.integerMax.description: An `aria-*` attribute needs an integer that is at most a maximum and was given something else.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

got.description: The value that was given, already rendered as source text (strings are quoted; `null` and `undefined` are spelled out). Do not add quotes around it.

ARIA2013.integerRange.description: An `aria-*` attribute needs an integer between a minimum and a maximum and was given something else.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

got.description: The value that was given, already rendered as source text (strings are quoted; `null` and `undefined` are spelled out). Do not add quotes around it.

ARIA2014.description: `aria-level` repeats the heading level the element already has, so it adds nothing and should be removed.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

ARIA2015.description: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set on a role that cannot be named by the author. It is a conformance error and will be removed.

attr.description: An ARIA attribute name, for example `aria-label`.

role.description: An ARIA role name, for example `region`.

COMP1004.description: A component received a child that its contract does not allow at all.

typeName.description: The kind of child found, a tag name or a JavaScript type name such as `object`.

scope.description: What the children belong to, for example `<ul>` or a component name.

COMP1005.description: A child matches more than one of the contract's child rules, so it is ambiguous which one applies.

typeName.description: The kind of child found, a tag name or a JavaScript type name such as `object`.

ruleNames.description: The names of the rules that matched, as a list.

scope.description: What the children belong to, for example `<ul>` or a component name.

COMP1006.description: A child rule requires a minimum number of matching children and fewer were given.

ruleName.description: The name the component gave a child rule in its contract.

scope.description: What the children belong to, for example `<ul>` or a component name.

COMP1007.description: A child rule allows a maximum number of matching children and more were given.

ruleName.description: The name the component gave a child rule in its contract.

scope.description: What the children belong to, for example `<ul>` or a component name.

COMP1008.first.description: A child rule requires its matching child to be the first child and it is not.

ruleName.description: The name the component gave a child rule in its contract.

scope.description: What the children belong to, for example `<ul>` or a component name.

COMP1008.last.description: A child rule requires its matching child to be the last child and it is not.

ruleName.description: The name the component gave a child rule in its contract.

scope.description: What the children belong to, for example `<ul>` or a component name.

COMP1009.description: The `as` prop named an element that this component does not allow. The allowed elements are listed.

tag.description: Element name without angle brackets, for example `nav`.

allowedAs.description: The elements allowed, as a list.

COMP1010.description: A configuration entry (for example a compound variant) refers to a variant that the component does not define.

label.description: Where in the configuration the problem was found, for example `compound[0]`.

COMP1011.description: A configuration entry sets a variant to a value the variant does not define. The valid values are listed.

label.description: Where in the configuration the problem was found, for example `compound[0]`.

valid.description: The valid values, as a list.

COMP1012.description: The `recipe` prop names a preset that does not exist.

key.description: The preset name that was not found.

COMP1013.description: A variant prop was given a value that is not one of the values defined for that variant.

SLOT1001.description: `as` and `asChild` were both given. They are mutually exclusive.

SLOT1002.required.description: `asChild` needs exactly one child element and none was given.

elementTerm.description: The adapter's word for an element, for example `React element` or `VNode`. A technical term; copy it verbatim.

SLOT1002.exceeded.description: `asChild` needs exactly one child element and more than one was given.

elementTerm.description: The adapter's word for an element, for example `React element` or `VNode`. A technical term; copy it verbatim.

count.description: A number of items; selects the plural form.

SLOT1003.description: `asChild` ignored children that were not elements (for example text). Only elements can be composed.

elementTerm.description: The adapter's word for an element, for example `React element` or `VNode`. A technical term; copy it verbatim.

count.description: A number of items; selects the plural form.

SLOT1004.description: `asChild` needs a render function as its children and something else was given.

received.description: The JavaScript type of what was given instead, for example `string`.

SLOT1005.description: `asChild` composed the component onto an element that is not in its list of allowed elements, so native behaviour may not work.

childTag.description: The tag of the element the child resolved to.

allowedAs.description: The elements allowed, as a list.

A11Y8100.description: An `<input>` has no accessible name (no label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).

A11Y8101.description: An `<input>` relies on its placeholder as its only name. A placeholder disappears as the user types and is not a reliable accessible name.

A11Y8102.description: A password `<input>` has no `autocomplete` value, so password managers cannot tell sign-in from sign-up.

A11Y8103.description: An `<input>` is both `required` and `readOnly`. A read-only field cannot be edited, so `required` can never be satisfied or violated.

A11Y8200.description: An `<a>` with an `href` has `role="button"`. It is announced as a button but still navigates when activated.

A11Y8201.description: An `<a>` has `aria-disabled`. Unlike a native control, a link stays focusable and clickable, so `aria-disabled` only changes what is announced.
